coreQuotaCard.quotaComesFromPaseoSUsageInterface: Quota comes from Paseo's usage interface, the same source as sidebar Usage. Paseo uses each provider's own login to read quota and caches each account for 5 minutes. The plugin reads no credentials and does not call vendor APIs directly.
coreQuotaCard.whileAPageIsViewingQuotaObservatory: While a page is viewing quota, Observatory records a reading every 10 minutes, including immediately on opening. It stops 30 minutes after the last view so Paseo does not query vendors when nobody is watching. Readings are kept for 40 days. Unchanged values get a heartbeat reading every 10 minutes; gaps over 15 minutes break the curve.
coreQuotaCard.ifAReadFailsAnAccountIs: If a read fails, an account is unavailable, or a reading is older than 15 minutes, the previous reading stays with its timestamp. Projections then serve only as reference, red warnings stop, and the dashboard chip shows "Reading 08:30".
coreQuotaCard.theVerticalLineOnTheProgressBar: The vertical line on the progress bar marks even usage pace and turns red when usage exceeds it. Windows shorter than a day, such as 5 hours, project exhaustion from at least 30 minutes of recent usage, warning only when it precedes reset. Weekly windows project the average pace so far through reset, after at least a tenth of the week has passed. Projections are reminders; bursts of usage can cause large errors.
coreQuotaCard.accountNamesMayBeEmailAddressesOnly: Account names may be email addresses. Only their hashes are stored. Multiple accounts from one source show as "Account 1", "Account 2", and redacted names.
coreQuotaCard.thePluginSSessionWithPaseoDisconnected: The plugin's session with Paseo disconnected, so quota updates are paused. It usually recovers automatically; reload the plugin if it persists

secondaryTokenBoard.tokensComeFromLocalClaudeCode: Tokens come from local Claude Code, Codex, Grok CLI, Pi, Kimi Code, and ZCode session logs, including custom providers based on them. Log folders are located through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME / GROK_HOME / KIMI_CODE_HOME / ZCODE_HOME / PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR in provider configuration, startup scripts, or Pi settings. Counting follows tools such as ccusage. Other provider logs are not yet supported; unavailable sources are hidden.
secondaryTokenBoard.includesAllLocalSessionsFromThese: Includes all local sessions from these providers, not only sessions started by Paseo, and links them to Paseo by session ID. Messages in resumed or forked sessions are deduplicated. Codex archived_sessions are included. Codex subagent threads, like Claude Code subagents, count toward their parent session. Sessions run in the system temporary folder, such as one-time scripts, are grouped under "Temporary folders" in "Project usage".
secondaryTokenBoard.grokCliRecordsEachTurnS: Grok CLI records each turn's usage once at the end (usage.json), so Grok counts by turn and has no individual call response duration. It contributes to totals, but not output rate or live throughput. Cache reads and writes are separated from its input. Observatory's own Grok insight analysis in temporary paseo-insight-* folders is excluded. Pi follows its own counting: replies, tool results with usage, and compaction and branch summaries. Kimi Code reads per-request usage.record entries, including subagents. ZCode reads completed steps from its local SQLite database and WAL, without counting duplicate message totals; cache reads and writes are separated from input. Missing usage and monetary cost are not estimated.
secondaryTokenBoard.providerUsageLinksLogsToPaseo: "Provider usage" links logs to Paseo sessions by session ID and then groups by provider. Custom providers sharing a log folder can therefore be separated. If a log folder belongs to only one custom provider, logs without a matching Paseo session also count toward it. Other unmatched logs, including terminal sessions and deleted sessions, are listed as "Unlinked sessions".
secondaryTokenBoard.dailyAndHourlyCountsUseThis: Daily and hourly counts use this device's time zone, including daylight saving transitions, like the statistics page. Logs are recorded by UTC hour and each hour is converted using its offset at the time.
secondaryTokenBoard.newInputCacheWriteCacheRead: New input + cache write + cache read = all context read by the model. Adding output gives the total. Cache hit rate = cache read ÷ total input.
secondaryTokenBoard.outputRateTpsOutputTokensResponse: Output rate (TPS) = output tokens ÷ response duration, including the wait for the first token. Live throughput spreads each call's output evenly across its response duration.
secondaryTokenBoard.onlyCountsModelsWorkingDirectoriesAnd: Only counts, models, working directories, and session IDs are stored. Prompts and output content are not stored. Costs are not estimated because prices vary by provider, proxy, or subscription even for the same model.

serverInsightAnalysis.m012: Every finding must cite at least one actual ref as evidence. Evidence may contain only existing refs from input records, never invented refs or prose. serverInsightAnalysis.m013: Use health=blocked only when there is clear evidence of an unresolved blocker. Use watch or healthy for normal exploration or recovered errors. Do not infer unreported total token use, money saved, or exact duration. Findings may be empty if there are no valuable issues, but include concrete strengths or nextActions based on visible evidence. Findings, strengths, and nextActions must not all be empty. Summary must state analytical conclusions, not preparation such as "read the full data first".

recap.title: Turn summary
recap.enabledHint: On: after each turn, {runner} writes the goal, progress and next step in one line
recap.disabledHint: Off. When on, AI writes one line after each turn: goal, progress, next step
recap.privacy: When on, about 10 seconds after a top-level agent's turn ends normally, the observatory sends the text of that turn and up to 8 turns before it (only your messages and the agent's, no tool output or reasoning; common credentials masked first; about 32 KB at most), with the session title, to the model chosen below, processed under that model's account. Masking is not exhaustive. Summaries are kept only in this host's plugin data (up to 300, for 30 days) and deleted when you turn this off.
recap.suggestionsHint: In the same call, guess the next message you might send. It shows as a button marked AI suggestion and goes out only when you tap it. None for credentials, deletions or production
recap.grokDetail: Low reasoning effort by default: quick and light. No tools; its session and search-index record are deleted afterwards
recap.providerNote: With a profile or another model, each summary starts a temporary read-only sub-agent in the agent's workspace and archives it when done; usage counts against that account. An agent gets at most one such summary every 30 minutes, for its latest turn, and shows its old summary as Old meanwhile. The archived sub-agents and their session records in the host and the provider stay in the workspace and add up; the plugin cannot delete them. The Grok CLI leaves none.
